title: Digi Tracker Suite
eyebrow: Case study · WordPress Telemetry & Repository Analytics
headline: Self-hosted WordPress telemetry and public repository analytics on shared hosting
lede: Between 25 August and 22 September 2026 I built Digi Tracker Suite for PluginizeLab, a self-hosted WordPress telemetry application and forked client SDK (`pluginizelab/digi-tracker-client`) that replaces Appsero. It collects opt-in heartbeats and deactivation feedback alongside daily public snapshots from wordpress.org. I made **all 40 commits** on `main` (22 with a Claude co-author trailer) and merged **both pull requests** on GitHub.

Two commits followed on 31 August for on-demand repository refreshes and the account overview dashboard. The repository was quiet from 1 to 19 September. sections.heading: Why build a self-hosted replacement for Appsero

blocks.text: From `DEPLOY.md` and `packages/digi-tracker-client/README.md`, the platform had to receive Appsero-protocol telemetry on infrastructure owned by PluginizeLab while meeting five constraints:

items: **Permanent ingest paths:** `/track`, `/deactivate` and `/tracking-skipped` are compiled into every released plugin copy and can never be changed once shipped.

**WordPress.org Guideline 7 compliance:** telemetry is strictly opt-in. The consent notice names Digi Tracker and links to our privacy policy, and the deactivation survey only fires when consent was granted.
**No third-party IP lookups:** upstream `appsero/client` queries `icanhazip.com` on every heartbeat. The fork removes that outbound call and derives country on our receiving server.

**Encrypted contact details at rest:** admin emails and names are encrypted with `APP_KEY`, paired with an HMAC blind index (`email_hash`) so records remain searchable without storing plaintext emails.
**Shared cPanel hosting:** the server runs on Namecheap shared hosting with SSH, MariaDB, and a single-line per-minute cron job.

sections.heading: The platform: durable ingest, queued reconciliation, and a Filament 5 panel

blocks.text: The WordPress SDK posts non-blocking requests (`'blocking' => false`), so a failed parse or dropped request is never retried by the client. `TrackController` and `DeactivateController` resolve the project from its UUID `hash`, write the raw request to `raw_payloads` before any interpretation, dispatch `ProcessTrackingPayload` to the database queue, and return `200 {"success": true}` immediately.

blocks.caption: Payloads land in `raw_payloads` first, then `ProcessTrackingPayload` and `SiteReconciler` update `sites`, `end_users`, and `site_reports` under a per-site lock.

blocks.text: In the panel, `Account` is the Filament 5 tenant (`/admin/{account-slug}/...`). Because Filament only scopes queries built by its own resources, an Eloquent global scope backed by `CurrentAccount` stays active so custom widgets and services cannot leak rows across tenants.

sections.heading: Ingest, metadata whitelist, and the nightly rollup (P1–P3)

blocks.text: P1 (`34638e9`) and P2 (`3b44fd7`) built the three ingest routes (`/track`, `/deactivate`, `/tracking-skipped`), the `extra[]` metadata whitelist, plugin inventory sync, GeoIP lookup, site status classification, anomaly detection, and the `daily_stats` rollup. P3 (`5ea4a31`, `4cd069e`) tried a hand-written TailAdmin Blade dashboard first and replaced it 15 minutes later with Filament 5 while keeping `DashboardMetrics` and the three bug fixes the first pass uncovered.

items: Form-encoded booleans
WordPress's `http_build_query` sends booleans as `"1"` and `""`. Standard Laravel `boolean` validation rejects empty strings, so `TrackRequest` reads them through explicit accessors.
Uncached project lookup

Caching an Eloquent `Project` model in the MySQL database cache store stripped the NUL bytes marking protected properties and unserialized as `__PHP_Incomplete_Class`. Caught during a live run and fixed in `3b44fd7` by querying uncached.
6-hour repeat window
Identical heartbeats within six hours update `last_seen_at` on `sites` without inserting a duplicate `site_reports` row, preventing a misconfigured cron from weighting one site multiple times.
Reactivation on the deactivation row
`sites` holds current state only. Stamping `reactivated_at` on the `deactivations` row lets `daily_stats` answer how many sites returned on a past date.

sections.heading: Forking appsero/client and closing two upstream consent holes (P4)

blocks.text: Commit `d77d96f` forked `appsero/client` v2.0.4 (MIT) into `packages/digi-tracker-client` under GPL-2.0-or-later. As documented in `packages/digi-tracker-client/README.md`, `dokan-lite` bundles `appsero/client` unscoped in the global `Appsero\` namespace behind `if ( ! class_exists( 'Appsero\Client' ) )`. Keeping that namespace on a site running Dokan would cause Dokan's unmodified client to load first and silently send our plugin's telemetry to Appsero's servers.

sections.heading: Analytics depth, GDPR erasure, and a single-choke-point email layer (P5–P6)

blocks.text: Commits `3550c54`, `9d1153f`, and `11e74aa` added the reproducible demo generator (`telemetry:seed-demo --seed`), which drives synthetic payloads through `SiteReconciler` rather than bulk-inserting rows, and `telemetry:forget`, which deletes a site or email across `sites`, `raw_payloads` (which sits outside foreign keys), and any `end_users` left owning zero sites.

P5 (`2042ba9`) added the project Reports page: version adoption stacked by percentage share rather than raw count, churn by theme calculated as a rate (excluding themes with fewer than 5 installs), and CSV exports with explicit per-call-site column lists so aggregate-only plugin inventories can never be exported.

P6 (`4ae69f7`) placed four email surfaces (deactivation auto-responder, deactivation forward to author, weekly Monday digest, and per-project branding) behind a single `Mailer` service. Because telemetry opt-in is consent to be measured rather than marketed to, the auto-responder fires only when a user typed a comment in the deactivation dialog, once per person per project. Unsubscribe links require no login, support RFC 8058 one-click `POST`, and store suppressions by HMAC blind index in `email_suppressions`.

sections.heading: Deploying to Namecheap cPanel: four assumptions the server broke

blocks.text: Deploying to `space.pluginizelab.com` on 27 August (`0ae456f` and `DEPLOY.md` section 0a) exposed four differences between local development (MySQL 9 on Herd) and the production Namecheap shared host (CloudLinux, LiteSpeed, MariaDB 11.4.12 behind Cloudflare):

blocks.caption: Measured on 27 Aug 2026 (`DEPLOY.md` section 0a). Proxied POSTs died mid-connection with curl exit codes 35/55/56 and no HTTP status while GET requests succeeded.

items: Cloudflare dropped half of POSTs

Because the SDK sends fire-and-forget POSTs, dropped `/track` requests silently under-counted installs and broke half of Livewire's panel updates. The ingest hostname is therefore DNS-only (`A` record to `198.54.116.227`), and `config/proxies.php` trusts Cloudflare's IP ranges rather than `'*'`.
MariaDB defaulted to MyISAM

Migrations failed on utf8mb4 1000-byte key limits. Worse, MyISAM lacks `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` row locks and transactions, which would have let overlapping per-minute queue workers send duplicate auto-responders and fired `DB::afterCommit()` prematurely. `config/database.php` now pins `'engine' => env('DB_ENGINE', 'InnoDB')`.
Split document root

cPanel locks the subdomain root to `~/space.pluginizelab.com`. `deploy/deploy.sh` keeps the application outside the web root at `~/digi-tracker`, copies `public/` into the docroot with rewritten `index.php` paths, and copies `public/build/` to both locations so Blade's `@vite` manifest check and the web server agree.
PHP 8.3 via CloudLinux handler

`/opt/cpanel/ea-php*` stopped at 8.2 and `selectorctl --domain` silently failed to create its CageFS directory. PHP 8.3.33 lived under `/opt/alt/php83`, pinned per-docroot via `AddHandler application/x-httpd-alt-php83___lsphp .php` in `.htaccess`.

blocks.caption: TrackController writes `raw_payloads` and returns 200 before `ProcessTrackingPayload` reconciles the site in the background.

sections.heading: Putting the public wordpress.org record beside private telemetry

blocks.text: Commits `8d7889e`, `5cda5a6`, `fa34b5f`, `938ee2c`, and `937bd6c` added public repository intelligence. Until released plugins ship with the new SDK, private telemetry reads zero while the plugins on wordpress.org already have years of history. Leading with the public Repository tab and placing tracked installs over public `active_installs` gives the true opt-in rate.

sections.heading: Client-side navigation, split auth pages, and OpenAI dark neutrals

blocks.text: On 28 August (`5c0f6ac`, `0f492c5`) I added transactional organisation sign-up (gated by `TELEMETRY_REGISTRATION`), password reset without account-enumeration leaks, and Livewire `wire:navigate` (`spa()`) across the panel with auth routes excluded and hover prefetching disabled so hovering a tab never triggers live requests to wordpress.org.
On 20 September (`30d3e18`, `392df1a`, `67f0478`, `f1a58d2`) I redesigned the authentication screens and panel typography:

items: **Split auth layout (`30d3e18`):** `/login`, `/register`, and `/password-reset/*` place the brand and a 28rem form column on the left and a muted looping video (`public/media/auth.mp4` with `auth-poster.jpg`, paused under `prefers-reduced-motion`) pinned on the right above 1024px.

**Local variable fonts (`392df1a`):** Replaced Filament's Bunny Fonts Inter request with self-hosted `@fontsource-variable/albert-sans` for body copy and `@fontsource-variable/outfit` for headings and KPI stat values.

**Dark by default on OpenAI neutrals (`67f0478`):** Remapped Filament's `--gray-*` tokens on `html.dark` to the `openai.com/codex` neutral scale. Auth pages force `.dark` before first paint and sync Filament's Alpine theme store in memory without overwriting a user's saved panel preference.

**Root auth URLs (`f1a58d2`):** Subclassed Filament's `Panel` (`App\Filament\AdminPanel`) to mount `/login`, `/register`, and `/password-reset/*` at the root while keeping `/admin/password-reset/reset` active so previously emailed signed links stay valid for their full hour.

sections.heading: The details a visitor never sees

items: 282 PHPUnit tests on real MySQL

`phpunit.xml` runs against MySQL (`digi_tracker_test`) rather than SQLite because JSON semantics differ. Base `TestCase` calls `Http::preventStrayRequests()`, stubbing wordpress.org with `metadata-viewer`'s real figures (`10 / 9 / 63 / 4,468`).
Read-only host preflight (`3b8b2fd`)
`deploy/preflight.sh` checks PHP version, `proc_open`, cron, and required extensions via `php -r` rather than `php -m | grep -q`, avoiding a `SIGPIPE` false failure under `set -o pipefail`.
GitHub Actions deploy pipeline (PRs #1–#2)

Merged on 22 September (`36c72f2`, `70682eb`). Runs the PHPUnit suite against `mariadb:11.4`, installs Composer dependencies so `@tailwindcss/vite` can resolve Filament's CSS in `vendor/`, executes `deploy/deploy.sh`, and smoke-tests `GET /login` (200) and `GET /.env` (404).
`composer dev` supervision (`6028cad`)

`CLAUDE.md` and `AGENTS.md` instruct agents to run `composer dev` (`artisan dev`) rather than `npm run dev`, after 7 queued `RefreshRepoStats` jobs sat at `attempts=0` for three weeks because Vite alone leaves `queue:listen` unstarted.

The Cloudflare POST arrival rates (10/25 on `/track`, 6/12 on Livewire updates vs 15/15 and 12/12 direct to origin) were measured on 27 August 2026 and recorded in `DEPLOY.md` section 0a. The test count (282 tests, 939 assertions) was measured by running `php artisan test` against PHP 8.3.36 and MySQL on 8 November 2026.
